import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

An upgrade replaces an app's code and keeps its state. The upgrade is an entry
in the app's own log; from that index on, every replica runs the new component
against the state the old one wrote
([Upgrades & migrations](/protocol/upgrades/) covers who may upgrade and
organization-wide upgrade runs).

<Aside type="caution">
  `calimero-sdk` has no state migrations in this version: there is no
  `#[app::migrate]` that rewrites stored data during an upgrade. The new code
  must read what the old code stored.
</Aside>

## Keep the state readable

State lives under keys derived from the `#[app::state]` field names and the
table and record layouts ([Tables & Collections](/build/collections/)):

- **Safe:** new methods; new events and errors; new fields on the state struct
  (a new field is a new key range, empty until written); new tables; new
  indexes on a new table.
- **Not safe:** renaming a state field (its old data is left under the old
  name), changing a field's collection type or value type, or changing a
  record's key, fields or field types. Old rows would no longer decode as the
  new type.

When a shape has to change, add a new field or table beside the old one, write
new data there, and read the old one until it is empty.

## The state version

`#[app::state(version = N)]` records `N` in the app's ABI, so clients and the
node's upgrade gate can tell which state layout a bundle expects. Bump it when
the state's shape changes.

`mero-app-build abi-diff <old> <new>` lists what changed in the state section
(and in the methods, errors, events and the shapes of the types they name), and
`mero-sign sign --previous <last release>` refuses to sign a release that removes a state field or changes its
kind without bumping the version ([App interface](/build/app-abi/#check-a-new-version-against-the-last)).

## Test it against the shipped release

Keep each release's signed `.mpk` beside the crate and run a migration
scenario from it to the build under test: the steps before its
`{ "op": "upgrade" }` write state with the shipped code, the steps after read
it with the new code ([Testing apps](/build/testing/#upgrades-test-against-a-shipped-releases-state)).
[Ship your app's next release](/build/ship-v2/) walks through a release end to end:
the state change, the test, publishing, and upgrading one instance and then an
organization, with what to do about each refusal.
